airflow_graph.png.app_state: a local Airflow 2.10.4 on the LocalExecutor with a PostgreSQL metadata database, the image built from infra/Dockerfile, after `airflow dags test multimodal_etl 2026-09-15` ran the five tasks with no NewsData.io key and no Kaggle export, so the RSS feeds and the Open Graph pages of the FakeNewsNet articles were fetched over the network, NewsData.io turned itself off and Fakeddit came from the versioned sample
airflow_graph.png.data_source: the RSS feeds, FakeNewsNet and the versioned Fakeddit sample; the picture shows task names and outcomes, and no publication
airflow_graph.png.demonstrates_behaviour: the five tasks chain and every one of them ends green, which is what the DAG is for: the same functions the scripts call, run under an orchestrator that can retry one of them without replaying the others

dashboard-history.png.app_state: the dashboard started against a corpus this repository owns: two runs of the pipeline on the versioned Fakeddit sample, NewsData.io left without a key so it turns itself off, the RSS connector pointed at a port where nothing listens, and FakeNewsNet not selected
dashboard-history.png.data_source: data/samples/fakeddit_sample.tsv — 24 made-up rows that keep 9 of the 16 columns of the Kaggle export, and freely-licensed illustrations; no publisher's content is on screen
dashboard-history.png.demonstrates_behaviour: the second run collected as much as the first and added nothing to the database, and the validity rate is drawn against its own axis rather than flattened onto the one the duration in seconds needs

dashboard-sources.png.app_state: the dashboard started against a corpus this repository owns: two runs of the pipeline on the versioned Fakeddit sample, NewsData.io left without a key so it turns itself off, the RSS connector pointed at a port where nothing listens, and FakeNewsNet not selected
dashboard-sources.png.data_source: data/samples/fakeddit_sample.tsv — 24 made-up rows that keep 9 of the 16 columns of the Kaggle export, and freely-licensed illustrations; no publisher's content is on screen
dashboard-sources.png.demonstrates_behaviour: three sources, three outcomes, as the connectors classified them when the picture was taken: the one that delivered, the one turned off for want of an API key, and the RSS connector pointed at a port where nothing listens, shown as having answered with nothing because the connectors then caught their own request failures. The current code reports that connector as unreachable and counts it as a failed source
